sections.title: Container build recipe
sections.what: Builds a container with Python 3.9, the tesseract OCR tool, the Python packages, and all code, then starts the API on port 8000.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes deployment repeatable on other machines.
sections.watch_out: It copies every file in the build folder, including any real secrets file.

summary: A recipe that packages the backend into a container image with Python, the OCR tool, and the app code.
purpose: Lets the backend run the same way on any machine that can run containers.
how: Starts from a slim Python 3.9 image, sets the work folder, installs tesseract-ocr and curl, installs Python requirements, copies all project files, creates data and log folders, exposes port 8000, and starts uvicorn on main:app.
inputs: The backend folder contents and requirements.txt.
outputs: A container image that serves the API on port 8000.
risks: Copies every file in the build folder into the image, so a real settings file with secrets would be packaged. The start command loads main as a top-level module, which likely breaks the relative imports in the app.
debug: If the container exits at start, read its log for relative import errors. If OCR fails, check that tesseract is installed. Check that the data folders exist inside the container.
